jobs.title: Strategic Finance Lead - GTM & Product
jobs.description:
About AngelList
Private markets are the new public markets. The most important companies of this era are private, and almost no one can own them. What's missing is the financial system public markets spent a century building: exchanges, custodians, brokers, and ways for ordinary people to buy in. Private markets, now $28T, never had the equivalent. AngelList is building it.
The last decade of structural innovation in venture happened here: syndicates, SPVs at scale, Rolling Funds, scout programs. Today we have $200B+ in assets and 30,000+ startups funded on our platform. The rest of private markets is next. Funds is the software and services behind private funds, Nova is the banking network, Meridian is the wealth platform for accredited investors, and USVC is the brand behind a registered fund that lets anyone invest in venture.
Working here means an unusual amount of agency on a problem that matters. Titles are closer to suggestions, and there are about 200 of us building what private markets never had. Come build it with us.
 


About the Role:
Nova is AngelList's banking and payments network for private markets. Funds and investors both live on the network, and money (subscriptions, capital calls, distributions) moves between them inside it instead of through wires and PDFs. On top of those rails sits a growing menu of financial products: treasury and yield, credit, and a wealth layer that keeps an investor's capital working from one fund to the next.
We're looking for someone to own the economics of that product menu with the autonomy and scope of a division CFO. Your fingerprints should be visible on which products we build, how they're priced, and how fast they reach the market.
This is not a traditional finance role. Success is whether the business makes better decisions, ships the right products, and accelerates revenue.

Responsibilities:
- Own the Nova business narrative on financial performance, product economics, and outlook, including mastery of the Nova P&L and revenue model.

- Own the economics of the financial-product menu (deposits, treasury, payments, credit, and wealth) and bring the point of view on what to build next, how it is priced, and how it makes money.

- Drive revenue growth: own target-setting and go-to-market planning for new and existing products, and unlock adoption across every channel from direct GP sales, the Ark / fund-admin cross-sell to the LP surface.

- Model the unit economics that drive the call (NIM and float, lending spread and risk, referral and take-rate economics, AUM fees), and connect each product to payments volume, balances, and revenue.
What we’re looking for:
- 8+ years across strategic finance, banking, private markets, or corporate strategy, owning growth planning personally. The strongest fits come from fintech or neobank strategic finance, private-markets infrastructure, or banking and financial services turned operational.

- You reason natively in financial-product economics: deposits and float, lending spreads, referral and take-rate economics, AUM fees. You can tell a profitable product from a costly one.

- You form a clear point of view on what to build next, build conviction across product, GTM, and ops, and carry it to launch with pricing, packaging, and targets. You've killed a bet people believed in when the economics don't hold.

- You operate with broad scope and no playbook. You make senior judgment calls before the data is clean, shape your own mandate, and have a bias to action. You'd rather decide in days and correct course than spend weeks on a cleaner answer.

- You can distill a complex problem to the handful of points that move the decision, and you communicate it to executives in writing, in person, and in charts.

- You've built AI into how you work and expect it to reshape how finance operates. You want to be the person defining what that looks like here.
How success will be measured:
- Leadership has conviction on which financial product we build next, and why.

- The Nova leadership team plans from one model it trusts, with product economics, targets, and tradeoffs in one place.

- There's a clear, consistent narrative on financial performance and which growth levers to prioritize.

- Revenue grows: new and existing products show up in payments volume, balances, and revenue, with GTM unlocked across direct, Ark / fund-admin, and LP channels.
Working Here
If you don’t meet every requirement above, we still encourage you to apply. We value complementary strengths and operators who learn by doing.
We operate out of hubs in New York City and San Francisco. For most roles on those teams, we work from the office at least two days per week (Tuesdays and either Wednesday or Thursday).

Compensation:The compensation for this role consists of a competitive base salary, benefits, and equity package. The base salary for this role is $220,000+ annually but actual will vary based on a number of factors including a candidate’s professional background, experience, and location. Full details about our Total Rewards package will be provided during the recruitment process.
Benefits:We support your life both in and outside of work.

About the Role: 
Meridian Platform Securities LLC is a registered broker-dealer and placement agent built for the modern private markets. We work with fund managers, sponsors, and issuers to connect capital with opportunity, with the rigor, structure, and integrity that investors demand. Compliance is not an afterthought here. It is core infrastructure, and we are looking for a CCO who sees it that way too.
You will own compliance end to end. That means building and maintaining the regulatory framework that lets us grow confidently rather than reactively, serving as our Series 24 principal, and holding the primary relationship with FINRA, the SEC, and applicable state regulators. You will be a trusted partner to leadership and a strategic resource for the deal team. You will be our first in-house CCO, standing the program up and taking it over from a vendor handoff already in motion.
You'll be in the room when deals and new products take shape, so compliance moves at the same speed as the deal team, finding the creative compliant path to “yes” on deal timelines. The program you build will scale with the firm. You'll start with a lean team and a live exam already underway.

Responsibilities
- Serve as the firm's designated CCO under FINRA Rule 3130, own the Written Supervisory Procedures,

- Be the deal team's compliance partner: review and clear diligence, marketing materials, private placement memoranda, and investor communications, and pressure-test new product structures so they are built compliantly from day one, on deal timelines.

- Manage FINRA and SEC examinations, inquiries, and correspondence from first notice through resolution, and run the annual compliance review with findings to senior management.

- Own registration and licensing across jurisdictions (principals, registered reps, state blue sky), maintain books and records under SEC Rules 17a-3 and 17a-4, and manage outside counsel on regulatory matters.

- Administer the firm's AML/BSA program, and monitor FINRA, SEC, FinCEN, and state developments, translating them into policy before they become problems.
You may be a good fit if you
- Hold an active Series 24 in good standing and have 7+ years of compliance experience at a FINRA-registered broker-dealer, including 3+ years in a senior or lead compliance role (ideally an online BD or fintech).

- Know private placements, Regulation D, secondaries, and the mechanics of how placement agents operate.

- Have managed FINRA cycle exams and regulatory inquiries yourself, not just supported them.

- Want to be the first in-house compliance hire and build the program from early stages.

- Bonus: Experience with SPVs, fund administration, syndication platforms, or exempt offering structures.
Working Here
If you don’t meet every requirement above, we still encourage you to apply. We value complementary strengths and operators who learn by doing.
We operate out of hubs in New York City and San Francisco. For most roles on those teams, we work from the office at least two days per week (Tuesdays and either Wednesday or Thursday).

The base salary for this role is $285,000+ annually but actual will vary based on a number of factors including a candidate’s professional background, experience, and location. jobs.description:
About AngelList
Private markets are the new public markets. The most important companies of this era are private, and almost no one can own them. What's missing is the financial system public markets spent a century building: exchanges, custodians, brokers, and ways for ordinary people to buy in. Private markets, now $28T, never had the equivalent. AngelList is building it.
The last decade of structural innovation in venture happened here: syndicates, SPVs at scale, Rolling Funds, scout programs. Today we have $200B+ in assets and 30,000+ startups funded on our platform. The rest of private markets is next. Funds is the software and services behind private funds, Nova is the banking network, Meridian is the wealth platform for accredited investors, and USVC is the brand behind a registered fund that lets anyone invest in venture.
Working here means an unusual amount of agency on a problem that matters. Titles are closer to suggestions, and there are about 200 of us building what private markets never had. Come build it with us.
 


About the Role:
AngelList supports more than $200B in assets across 30,000+ funds and syndicates, with over $80B moved through our banking infrastructure. Our network includes 2,300+ GPs and 72,000+ LPs, and more than a decade of private-market transaction data sits underneath the platform.
The opportunity now is to turn that scale, knowledge, and customer trust into a stronger market position and a durable source of growth. We are looking for a senior, hands-on marketing leader to build the positioning, launch rhythm, campaigns, and distribution behind AngelList’s businesses.
You’ll start with Funds. AngelList supports everything from a founder’s first SPV to $500M institutional funds, but many of the firms we want to serve next formed their view of us years ago, when AngelList was best known as where emerging managers got started. Your first challenge is to change that perception without losing what made the brand valuable. Nova, the banking network underpinning private markets, comes next.
You’ll work directly with Product on what we are building and why it matters, with Sales on why important deals are won and lost, and with the GMs and operators who know our customers best. Your job is to turn what AngelList knows into positioning, proof, and programs that change how the market sees us—and ultimately change customer behavior, pipeline, and revenue.
This is a player-coach role. You’ll manage a growth marketer, lead contractors across SEO, production, and creative, and build the team as your work earns further investment. This is a role for a doer: you’ll write the positioning, build the campaigns, talk to customers, and lead important launches yourself.
For the right marketer, it is a rare amount of leverage.

What You’ll Own
- Shape the story. Develop positioning and messaging for AngelList and its businesses. Make sophisticated financial products easy to understand and hard to dismiss.

- Lead important launches. Own the narrative, enablement, content, distribution, and measurement around the product and company moments that matter.

- Turn proof into persuasion. Bring customer outcomes, institutional logos, migration results, product advantages, and market data into the buying process.

- Publish what AngelList knows. Turn proprietary data and in-house expertise into useful, opinionated work that GPs and LPs share with one another.

- Build durable distribution. Develop and test programs across content, customer networks, events, search, partnerships, and channels we have not tried yet.

- Partner deeply with Sales. Understand why we win, why we lose, and where the story breaks. Build marketing and enablement that improve those outcomes.

- Establish a consistent shipping rhythm. Put meaningful work into the market every week, learn from the response, and reinvest behind what works.

- Build the function. Manage internal and external contributors, set a high standard for the work, and add capabilities as the opportunity becomes clear.
What We’re Looking For
- You are an exceptional product marketer and writer. You can get deep into a complicated business, find the thing that matters, and explain it plainly.

- You have substantial experience in product, growth, or integrated B2B marketing, including positioning, launches, and campaigns you led end to end.

- You have managed marketers or external partners while continuing to produce important work yourself.

- You have marketed to sophisticated B2B buyers—such as funds, finance teams, or CFOs—where buying decisions are considered and the target market is specific enough to name.

- You care equally about story and distribution. You know that a strong narrative is only valuable if the right people encounter it.

- You have strong commercial instincts. You care whether the work changes customer behavior, creates qualified opportunities, and contributes to revenue, assets, or transaction volume.

- You create direction in ambiguous situations and become credible quickly by talking to customers, salespeople, product leaders, and operators.

- You use data with discipline without pretending attribution is more precise than it is.

- You have high standards, move quickly, and prefer doing excellent work to managing a large machine.
Working Here
If you don’t meet every requirement above, we still encourage you to apply. We value complementary strengths and operators who learn by doing.
AngelList has offices in a few cities, New York City and San Francisco. We have a hybrid in-office model: teammates come in at least 2 days per week (Tuesdays and either Wednesday or Thursday).
